key_insight: A single success metric hides critical operational weaknesses of AI agents; evaluating multiple reliability dimensions (consistency, robustness, failure predictability, error severity) gives a more actionable picture of real-world dependability.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high benchmark scores and frequent real-world failures by providing a structured way to measure and report agent reliability beyond aggregate accuracy.
method: Formalize key reliability dimensions: run-to-run consistency, perturbation robustness, predictability of failures, and bounded error severity.
Design metrics and evaluation protocols to quantify each dimension instead of a single success rate.
Apply the protocols across representative agents/benchmarks to reveal reliability blind spots masked by traditional scores.
impact: Enables practitioners to detect risky agents before deployment, prioritize robustness improvements, and adopt standard reliability reporting—leading to safer, more predictable AI systems.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing the four reliability dimensions for multiple agents (quickly shows tradeoffs and weaknesses).
Scatter plot of benchmark accuracy versus aggregate reliability score to illustrate the accuracy–reliability gap.
Timeline or run-sequence diagram showing run-to-run variability and intermittent failures across repeated trials.
Stacked bar or heatmap of error-severity distributions under perturbations to highlight worst-case impacts.
paper_title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
paper_authors: Stephan Rabanser, Sayash Kapoor, Peter Kirgis, Kangheng Liu, Saiteja Utpala
